title: Next step after the NAT-088 finding (restore-mode launchd alive, 20 of 23 boot tasks skipped, one job respawned): read the log of such a run without the two analyser flaws (dump records with transport holes are kept with exact hole ranges instead of refusing the boot; the kernel-format launchd System Event boot-task lines are read), and prepare the Stage A job set - the donor's Apple daemons minus wifid, backboardd and SpringBoard, plus the NAT-085 ps heartbeat - as a small root; analyser rows A1-A8 over per-label spawns/exits and the last ps list; host-test only, no phone action
acceptance: kl_reader.py reads every boot of a collector archive, merges the KL dumps of replay boots by offset (a different byte at the same offset is a conflict, never silently chosen), reports the exact hole ranges of the head and tail and the announced gap, and reads the real NAT-088 archive (second boot: the 8,192-byte head and 32,768-byte tail with the hole ranges the two ring-overrun drop records announce).

analyze_nat089.py reads the boot-task lines in the kernel System Event form and the ps heartbeat lists, builds the per-label table (spawns, exits with the reason text, alive in the last ps list) for the labels of a built LaunchDaemons directory, and decides rows A1-A8 as documented; over the real NAT-088 text it reads exactly the 20 skipped and 3 run boot tasks and the com.nat085.ps heartbeat (3 spawns, pids 12-14), and row A7/A4-type outcomes follow from hand-built inputs only (no Stage A text exists yet).

The Stage A small root builds with tools/ios/build_pid1_chain.py --jobs --skip-job wifid/backboardd/SpringBoard --job com.nat085.ps.plist; its LaunchDaemons directory holds the 19 Apple plists and the heartbeat, with the self-starting jobs (RunAtLoad or KeepAlive true) listed from the plists themselves. Nothing here measures the phone.
steps: Tests over the real NAT-088 archive and hand-built inputs
